title: M2B Mains · Paper II · Section B · Science and Technology (75M) › M2B.5 Environment and Health

syllabus_leaves.wording: Environment Challenges: Global Warming, Climate Change, Acid Rain, Ozone Layer Depletion, Ocean Acidification
Environmental Initiatives: Recent International Initiatives, Protocols, Conventions to tackle Climate Change with special reference to India’s Participation and Role
International initiatives, protocols and conventions on climate change
Sustainable Development: Meaning, Nature, Scope, Components and Goals of Sustainable Development
Meaning, nature and scope of sustainable development
Health Issues: Recent Trends in Disease Burden and Epidemic and Pandemic Challenges in India
Preparedness and Response: Healthcare Delivery and Outcomes in India
Recent Public Health Initiatives and Programmes

official_questions.stem: The commonly used medicine for typhoid is
official_questions.core_fact: Typhoid (Salmonella Typhi) was classically treated with chloramphenicol (Chloromycetin); today fluoroquinolones/ceftriaxone/azithromycin are used.

statements.t: The commonly used medicine for typhoid is a sulpha drug.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The commonly used medicine for typhoid is chloromycetin.
The commonly used medicine for typhoid is chloroquin.
The commonly used medicine for typhoid is ascorbic acid.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

official_questions.rule: Typhoid: chloramphenicol (classic); malaria: chloroquine; TB: rifampicin/isoniazid.

official_questions.stem: Insufficient dietary iodine causes a/an
official_questions.core_fact: Dietary iodine deficiency enlarges the thyroid (simple goitre); severe deficiency in pregnancy causes cretinism in the child.

statements.t: Insufficient dietary iodine causes a/an giant.
statements.fact: Gigantism is due to excess GH.

statements.t: Insufficient dietary iodine causes a/an cretin.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Cretinism is a congenital outcome; the keyed dietary effect is goitre.

statements.t: Insufficient dietary iodine causes a/an enlarged thyroid.
Insufficient dietary iodine causes a/an small thyroid.

official_questions.rule: Iodine -> goitre; NIDDCP (universal salt iodisation).
official_questions.key_note: Cretinism can also follow severe iodine deficiency (in utero); key 'enlarged thyroid' is the standard answer. Kept.

official_questions.stem: A drug used in the prevention and control of malaria is
official_questions.core_fact: Chloroquine is a classic antimalarial for prevention and treatment (resistance now common; artemisinin combinations used).

statements.t: A drug used in the prevention and control of malaria is Heterozine.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: A drug used in the prevention and control of malaria is Chloroquine.
A drug used in the prevention and control of malaria is Piperazine.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: A drug used in the prevention and control of malaria is Resorcinol.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

official_questions.rule: Malaria: chloroquine, ACT; filaria: DEC; worms: albendazole/piperazine.

official_questions.stem: The country that launched Global greenhouse satellite, IBUKI, to estimate the carbon dioxide and methane present in the atmosphere above the Earth is
official_questions.core_fact: IBUKI (GOSAT), launched by Japan (JAXA) on 23 Jan 2009, measures atmospheric CO2 and methane.

statements.t: The country that launched the greenhouse satellite IBUKI is Russia.
The country that launched the greenhouse satellite IBUKI is U.S.A..
The country that launched the greenhouse satellite IBUKI is China.
The country that launched the greenhouse satellite IBUKI is Japan.

official_questions.rule: GHG satellites: GOSAT/IBUKI (Japan 2009), OCO-2 (USA 2014), TanSat (China 2016).

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of epidemic ?
official_questions.core_fact: Epidemics are classified as common-source (point/continuous), propagated, seasonal and cyclical (modern trends).

statements.t: Propagated epidemic is a type of epidemic.
Seasonal epidemic is a type of epidemic.
Cyclical epidemic is a type of epidemic.
All the above is a type of epidemic.

official_questions.rule: Epidemic types: common-source (single/continuous), propagated, slow (modern), seasonal, cyclical.

official_questions.stem: Mosquito repellants mainly contain
official_questions.core_fact: Mosquito repellents mainly contain DEET, synthetic pyrethroids (allethrin, transfluthrin) or natural oils (citronella); none of the offered inorganic salts is the active agent.

statements.t: Mosquito repellents mainly contain Calcium phosphate.
Mosquito repellents mainly contain Sodium hydrogen sulphate.
Mosquito repellents mainly contain Calcium hydrogen phosphate.
Mosquito repellents mainly contain Ammonium bisulphate.

official_questions.rule: Repellents: DEET, pyrethroids (allethrin), citronella; vector control under NCVBDC.
official_questions.key_note: Deleted by APPSC in the final key (no correct option).

official_questions.stem: Few decades ago, DDT was used to kill mosquitoes. Later, in the recent years, it became very difficult to kill mosquitoes using DDT. Which principle explains the immunity of mosquitoes from DDT?
official_questions.core_fact: DDT resistance in mosquitoes arose by natural selection: resistant variants survived and reproduced.

statements.t: The principle explaining mosquitoes' immunity to DDT is the Theory of Natural Intervention.
The principle explaining mosquitoes' immunity to DDT is the Theory of Immunity.
statements.fact: Resistance is selected genetic variation, not acquired immunity.

statements.t: The principle explaining mosquitoes' immunity to DDT is the Predator-Prey theory.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The principle explaining mosquitoes' immunity to DDT is the Theory of Natural Selection.

official_questions.rule: Resistance (DDT, antibiotics) = natural selection.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is a viral disease?
official_questions.core_fact: Herpes is caused by herpes simplex virus; malaria is protozoan (Plasmodium); typhoid (Salmonella Typhi) and diphtheria (Corynebacterium) are bacterial.

statements.t: Malaria is a viral disease.
Typhoid is a viral disease.
Herpes is a viral disease.
Diphtheria is a viral disease.

official_questions.rule: Viral: herpes, polio, measles, dengue; bacterial: typhoid, TB, diphtheria; protozoan: malaria.

official_questions.stem: Kigali Agreement modifies which of these previous multi lateral agreements
official_questions.core_fact: The Kigali Amendment (Oct 2016, in force 2019) amended the Montreal Protocol to phase down HFCs; India's freeze 2028, 85% cut by 2047.

statements.t: The Kigali Agreement modifies the Kyoto Protocol.
statements.fact: Kigali amends the Montreal Protocol, not Kyoto.

statements.t: The Kigali Agreement modifies the Montreal Protocol.
The Kigali Agreement modifies the Bali Action Plan.
statements.fact: Bali Action Plan is a UNFCCC roadmap; Kigali amends Montreal.

statements.t: The Kigali Agreement modifies the Paris Agreement.
statements.fact: Paris is UNFCCC; Kigali amends Montreal.

official_questions.rule: Kigali (2016) = Montreal Protocol amendment on HFCs; Doha (2012) = Kyoto amendment.

official_questions.stem: Which is the first ‘carbon neutral’ international airport in Asia-Pacific?
official_questions.core_fact: Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport became the first airport in Asia-Pacific to achieve 'carbon neutral' (ACI ACA Level 3+) status in 2016.

statements.t: The first carbon-neutral international airport in Asia-Pacific is Chatrapathi Shivaji International Airport.
statements.fact: Mumbai was not first; Delhi IGI was.

statements.t: The first carbon-neutral international airport in Asia-Pacific is Kempegowda International Airport.
The first carbon-neutral international airport in Asia-Pacific is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport.
The first carbon-neutral international airport in Asia-Pacific is Indira Gandhi International Airport.

official_questions.rule: Delhi IGI first carbon-neutral in Asia-Pacific (2016); Cochin = world's first fully solar-powered airport (2015).

official_questions.stem: Choose the correct Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDC) in carbon emissions under the Paris Climate Change Agreement set by India
official_questions.core_fact: India's 2015 INDC: reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 33-35% below 2005 levels by 2030; 40% non-fossil power capacity; 2.5-3 GtCO2e sink (updated 2022 NDC: 45%, 50%).

statements.t: India's INDC under the Paris Agreement is a cut of 33-35 Per cent below 2005 levels by 2030.
India's INDC under the Paris Agreement is a cut of 20-25 Per cent below 1990 levels by 2020.
statements.fact: India's base year is 2005 and target year 2030.

statements.t: India's INDC under the Paris Agreement is a cut of 23-25 Per cent below 2000 levels by 2020.
statements.fact: India's INDC: 33-35% below 2005 by 2030 (its 2009 Copenhagen pledge was 20-25% below 2005 by 2020).

statements.t: India's INDC under the Paris Agreement is a cut of 15-20 Per cent below 1990 levels by 2030.

official_questions.rule: India NDC: 2015 = 33-35%/40%; 2022 update = 45% intensity, 50% non-fossil capacity; net zero 2070.
official_questions.key_note: The stem says 'carbon emissions'; the INDC target is emission intensity of GDP, not absolute emissions.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not included in the concept of Sustainable Development?
options: aspirations of the present generations without compromising on the needs of the future generations
constant or rising overall capital assets
official_questions.core_fact: Sustainable development = meeting present needs without compromising future generations, environmental conservation and a non-declining (constant or rising) capital stock; 'climatic changes over time' is a phenomenon, not part of the concept.

statements.t: aspirations of the present generations without compromising on the needs of the future generations is not included in the concept of sustainable development.
statements.d: aspirations of the present generations without compromising on the needs of the future generations

statements.t: environmental conservation is not included in the concept of sustainable development.
constant or rising overall capital assets is not included in the concept of sustainable development.
statements.d: constant or rising overall capital assets

statements.t: climatic changes over time is not included in the concept of sustainable development.

official_questions.rule: SD components: intergenerational equity, environment, non-declining capital; climate change is a challenge, not a component.

official_questions.stem: In respect of environmental protection, which of the following statements is true?
options: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury
environmental protection is an expensive proposition
It is difficult to assess the damages due to violation of ecological and environmental limits
economic growth will necessarily suffer in the short-run if environment protection measures are implemented
official_questions.key: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury
official_questions.core_fact: Per key, at India's present level of development environmental protection is a necessity, not a luxury.

statements.t: In respect of environmental protection, the true statement is: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury.
statements.d: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury

statements.t: In respect of environmental protection, the true statement is: environmental protection is an expensive proposition.
statements.d: environmental protection is an expensive proposition
statements.fact: Key: protection is not a luxury; costs are outweighed by damage avoided.

statements.t: In respect of environmental protection, the true statement is: It is difficult to assess the damages due to violation of ecological and environmental limits.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.d: It is difficult to assess the damages due to violation of ecological and environmental limits
statements.fact: Key: option 1; (damage valuation is hard but possible).

statements.t: In respect of environmental protection, the true statement is: economic growth will necessarily suffer in the short-run if environment protection measures are implemented.
statements.d: economic growth will necessarily suffer in the short-run if environment protection measures are implemented

official_questions.rule: Environment–growth: 'necessarily' trade-offs are F.

official_questions.stem: In the developing world the largest polluter in the terms of CO2 emissions is
official_questions.core_fact: China is the largest CO2 emitter in the developing world (and the world, since 2006); India is third globally.

statements.t: In the developing world the largest polluter in terms of CO2 emissions is China.
In the developing world the largest polluter in terms of CO2 emissions is India.
In the developing world the largest polluter in terms of CO2 emissions is North Korea.
In the developing world the largest polluter in terms of CO2 emissions is Brazil.

official_questions.rule: Emitter ranks (total): China > USA > India; per-capita India is low.

official_questions.stem: The United Nations Convention on Climate Change held at Paris in December, 2015 agreed on
official_questions.core_fact: At COP21 (Paris, Dec 2015) parties agreed that each country sets its own Nationally Determined Contributions (bottom-up).

statements.t: The UN climate conference at Paris in December 2015 agreed on Centrally determined contributions.
statements.fact: The Paris Agreement rests on Nationally Determined Contributions.

statements.t: The UN climate conference at Paris in December 2015 agreed on Capacity based determination of contributions.
statements.fact: The Paris Agreement rests on Nationally Determined Contributions.

statements.t: The UN climate conference at Paris in December 2015 agreed on UNO determined contributions.
statements.fact: The Paris Agreement rests on Nationally Determined Contributions.

statements.t: The UN climate conference at Paris in December 2015 agreed on Nationally determined contributions.

official_questions.rule: Kyoto = top-down binding targets (Annex I); Paris = NDCs by each country.

official_questions.stem: In which place of Andhra Pradesh, the government decided to establish Kidney Research Centre & Super Specialty Hospital with an outlay of Rs. 50.00 Cr.?
official_questions.core_fact: AP decided (2019) to set up a Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital at Palasa, Srikakulam (Uddanam CKDu belt), outlay Rs 50 crore.

statements.t: AP decided to establish the Kidney Research Centre & Super Specialty Hospital (Rs 50 crore) at Palasa, Srikakulam.

official_questions.rule: Uddanam (Srikakulam) CKDu -> Palasa kidney hospital & research centre (opened 2023).

official_questions.stem: The Drug and Magic remedies Act, 1954 prohibit
official_questions.core_fact: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act 1954 prohibits advertisements of drugs/magic remedies claiming to cure listed diseases.

statements.t: The Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, 1954 prohibits publication of objectionable advertisements.

official_questions.rule: 1954 Act = ads; Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940 = manufacture/sale.

official_questions.stem: Edema is a typical clinical feature of which disease?
official_questions.core_fact: Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) typically shows oedema (swelling), unlike marasmus (protein-energy deficiency, wasting without oedema).

statements.t: Edema is a typical clinical feature of Kwashiorkor.

official_questions.rule: Oedema -> kwashiorkor; severe wasting without oedema -> marasmus.

official_questions.stem: ________ is a leading cause of maternal mortality and is showing an increasing trend in Andhra Pradesh, affecting infants, children, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age.
official_questions.core_fact: NFHS-4/5 show high and rising anaemia among children, adolescent girls and women in AP; anaemia is a leading indirect cause of maternal mortality.

statements.t: Anaemia is a leading cause of maternal mortality and is showing an increasing trend in Andhra Pradesh.

official_questions.rule: Anaemia Mukt Bharat (2018) targets 6-59 months children, adolescents, pregnant/lactating women.

official_questions.stem: ________ condition is a result of plaque buildup in the arteries
official_questions.core_fact: Coronary artery disease results from atherosclerotic plaque narrowing the coronary arteries.

statements.t: Coronary artery disease is a result of plaque buildup in the arteries.

official_questions.rule: Plaque in arteries = atherosclerosis -> CAD/IHD.

official_questions.stem: As per NFHS-4 the IMR rate in Andhra Pradesh was
official_questions.core_fact: NFHS-4 (2015-16) recorded an IMR of about 35 per 1,000 live births in Andhra Pradesh.

statements.t: As per NFHS-4 the IMR in Andhra Pradesh was 35.

official_questions.rule: Distinguish NFHS IMR (survey) from SRS IMR; give the year with the figure.

official_questions.stem: A measure of land and water needed to produce the resources we consume and to dispose the waste we produce is known as
official_questions.core_fact: Ecological footprint = the biologically productive land and water area required to produce the resources a population consumes and to absorb its wastes (Wackernagel & Rees, 1990s).

statements.t: A measure of land and water needed to produce the resources we consume and dispose the waste we produce is Ecological foot print.

official_questions.rule: Ecological footprint (area) vs carbon footprint (GHG) vs carrying capacity (max population).

official_questions.stem: The major greenhouse gas produced from low land rice cultivation is
official_questions.core_fact: Flooded (lowland) paddy fields are anaerobic; methanogenic archaea release methane.

statements.t: The major greenhouse gas produced from lowland rice cultivation is methane.

official_questions.rule: Paddy & ruminants -> CH4; fertilised soils -> N2O.

official_questions.stem: In which year was 'Arogyasree' started in A.P?
official_questions.core_fact: Rajiv Aarogyasri health insurance scheme for BPL families started in undivided AP on 1 April 2007 (pilot in Mahabubnagar, Anantapur, Srikakulam); now Dr YSR Aarogyasri.

statements.t: 'Arogyasree' was started in AP in 2007.

official_questions.rule: Aarogyasri 2007 (AP) preceded RSBY (2008) and PM-JAY (2018).

official_questions.stem: In 2012, which country of the followings was with the lowest GHG Emitters on per capita basis is
official_questions.core_fact: In 2012 India's per-capita GHG emissions (~1.9-2.5 t CO2e) were far below the US, EU, China and Russia among large emitters.

statements.t: In 2012 India was the lowest per-capita GHG emitter among the listed countries.

official_questions.rule: India: 3rd largest total emitter, but low per capita - total vs per capita trap.

official_questions.stem: The International Day For 'The Preservation Of Ozone layer' is
official_questions.core_fact: The UN General Assembly (1994) designated 16 September, the date the Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987, as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.

statements.t: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is 16 September.

official_questions.rule: Ozone Day 16 Sep (Montreal 1987); Vienna Convention 1985; Kigali Amendment 2016 (HFCs).

official_questions.stem: Among the Millennium Development Goals, which target set for 2015 was achieved by India ?
official_questions.core_fact: Per India's MDG Report 2015 (MoSPI), India met the poverty-halving target of MDG 1 (headcount 21.9% in 2011-12 vs target 23.9%); universal primary education, maternal health (MMR target 109) and environmental targets were not fully achieved.

statements.t: Among MDGs, India achieved the 2015 target of Eradicating Extreme Poverty and Hunger.
Among MDGs, India achieved the 2015 target of Achieving Universal Primary Education.
statements.fact: Primary completion/literacy targets were not fully met.

statements.t: Among MDGs, India achieved the 2015 target of Improving Maternal Health.
Among MDGs, India achieved the 2015 target of Ensuring Environment Sustainability.
statements.fact: Sanitation and other targets were missed.

official_questions.rule: India MDGs: poverty met; gender parity in schooling met; MMR, IMR, sanitation missed.
official_questions.key_note: Strictly only the poverty sub-target of MDG 1 was met (hunger/underweight target was missed).

official_questions.stem: Out of 8 Millennium Development Goals, how many goals are directly related to health ?
official_questions.core_fact: Of 8 MDGs, three are directly health-related: Goal 4 (child mortality), Goal 5 (maternal health), Goal 6 (HIV/AIDS, malaria, other diseases).

statements.t: Out of 8 MDGs, 1 goals are directly related to health.
Out of 8 MDGs, 2 goals are directly related to health.
Out of 8 MDGs, 3 goals are directly related to health.
Out of 8 MDGs, 4 goals are directly related to health.
statements.fact: Three (4, 5, 6); hunger is part of Goal 1.

official_questions.rule: MDGs: 1 poverty/hunger, 2 education, 3 gender, 4 child, 5 maternal, 6 diseases, 7 environment, 8 partnership.

official_questions.stem: The Sustainable Development Goals India Index 2018 is based on how many main goals ?
official_questions.core_fact: The SDGs have 17 goals; NITI Aayog's baseline SDG India Index (Dec 2018) scored States on 13 of them (62 indicators), with Goal 17 qualitatively.

statements.t: The SDG India Index 2018 is based on 17 main goals.
The SDG India Index 2018 is based on 18 main goals.
The SDG India Index 2018 is based on 19 main goals.
The SDG India Index 2018 is based on 20 main goals.

official_questions.rule: SDG India Index: 2018 baseline 13 goals/62 indicators; 2019-20 16 goals; 2020-21 onwards 16 + Goal 17 qualitative.
official_questions.key_note: The 2018 baseline index actually computed scores on 13 of the 17 goals; key (17) kept as the goal framework.

official_questions.stem: Which two States are the front runners in the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals in 2018 ?
official_questions.core_fact: SDG India Index 2018: Kerala and Himachal Pradesh topped (score 69); Tamil Nadu 66; lowest were UP, Bihar, Assam.

statements.t: The two front runners in SDG achievement in 2018 are Kerala and Himachal Pradesh.
The two front runners in SDG achievement in 2018 are Assam and Bihar.
statements.fact: Assam and Bihar were in the 'aspirant' bottom group.

statements.t: The two front runners in SDG achievement in 2018 are Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
The two front runners in SDG achievement in 2018 are Punjab and Haryana.

official_questions.rule: SDG Index categories: achiever 100, front-runner 65-99, performer 50-64, aspirant <50.

official_questions.stem: Child mortality implies children dying before their
official_questions.core_fact: Child (under-five) mortality = deaths before the 5th birthday per 1,000 live births; infant mortality = before the 1st birthday.

statements.t: Child mortality implies children dying before their 1st birthday.
statements.fact: Death before the 1st birthday is infant mortality.

statements.t: Child mortality implies children dying before their 2nd birthday.
statements.fact: Child mortality cut-off is the 5th birthday.

statements.t: Child mortality implies children dying before their 3rd birthday.
statements.fact: Child mortality cut-off is the 5th birthday.

statements.t: Child mortality implies children dying before their 5th birthday.

official_questions.rule: Neonatal <28 days; infant <1 yr; under-five <5 yrs; MMR per 1 lakh live births.

official_questions.stem: On which date is ‘World Environment Day’ celebrated ?
official_questions.core_fact: World Environment Day is 5 June (UNGA 1972, from the Stockholm Conference opening on 5 June 1972; first observed 1974).

statements.t: World Environment Day is celebrated on 4th June.
World Environment Day is celebrated on 5th June.
World Environment Day is celebrated on 6th June.
World Environment Day is celebrated on 7th June.

official_questions.rule: June days: 5 Environment, 8 Oceans, 17 Desertification, 22 April Earth Day.

official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) led by National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti was launched at COP28 in New Delhi.
II. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) is a unique alliance covering 275+ global river cities in 11 countries.
III. The Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) is the first of its kind in the world.
Which of the above given statements is/are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: The GRCA, led by India's NMCG (Ministry of Jal Shakti), was launched at COP28 in Dubai (Dec 2023); it covers 275+ river cities in 11 countries and is described as the first of its kind.

statements.t: The GRCA led by NMCG under the Ministry of Jal Shakti was launched at COP28 in New Delhi.
statements.fact: GRCA was launched at COP28 in Dubai.

statements.t: The GRCA covers 275+ global river cities in 11 countries.
The GRCA is the first of its kind in the world.

official_questions.rule: COP venues: COP27 Sharm el-Sheikh, COP28 Dubai, COP29 Baku, COP30 Belem.

official_questions.stem: What is the key characteristic of black carbon that accelerates global warming ?
options: It is a type of methane
It is a short-lived pollutant produced by incomplete combustion
It directly depletes the ozone layer
official_questions.key: It is a short-lived pollutant produced by incomplete combustion
official_questions.core_fact: Black carbon (soot) from incomplete combustion is a short-lived climate pollutant (days-weeks) that absorbs sunlight and darkens snow/ice.

statements.t: Black carbon is a type of methane.
statements.fact: Black carbon is particulate soot; methane is a gas (both are SLCPs).

statements.t: Black carbon is a short-lived pollutant produced by incomplete combustion.
Black carbon is released by CFCs.
statements.fact: Black carbon comes from burning fuels/biomass.

statements.t: Black carbon directly depletes the ozone layer.
statements.fact: Ozone depletion is by CFCs/halons; BC warms by absorption.

official_questions.rule: SLCPs: BC, CH4, tropospheric O3, HFCs.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following countries is/are legally bound by the emissions reduction targets set by the Paris Agreement ?
official_questions.core_fact: The Paris Agreement (2015) is a binding treaty but its emission targets (NDCs) are nationally determined and not legally binding; parties are bound only to prepare, communicate and pursue NDCs. (US withdrawal effective Jan 2026.)

statements.t: The United States and China are legally bound by the Paris Agreement's emission reduction targets.
statements.fact: No party's NDC target is legally binding.

statements.t: India is legally bound by the Paris Agreement's emission reduction targets.
statements.fact: India's NDC is not legally binding.

statements.t: The European Union is legally bound by the Paris Agreement's emission reduction targets.
statements.fact: EU's binding targets come from EU law, not Paris.

statements.t: None of these countries is legally bound by the Paris Agreement's emission reduction targets.

official_questions.rule: Kyoto = binding targets (Annex I); Paris = binding procedure, non-binding targets.
official_questions.key_note: Time note: the US withdrew again (notice Jan 2025, effective Jan 2026); irrelevant to the key.

official_questions.stem: How many core missions are included in India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) ?
official_questions.core_fact: NAPCC (2008) has eight national missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge.

statements.t: NAPCC includes 5 core missions.
NAPCC includes 8 core missions.
NAPCC includes 12 core missions.
NAPCC includes 10 core missions.
statements.fact: NAPCC has 8 missions (a 9th on human health was added later).

official_questions.rule: NAPCC = 8 core missions; later additions (e.g. Climate Change & Human Health) are not 'core'.

official_questions.stem: What is the "dual burden" India faces in public health ?
options: Rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases
Lack of insurance and financial access
High rates of both obesity and malnutrition
official_questions.key: High rates of both obesity and malnutrition
official_questions.core_fact: APPSC key: 'dual burden' = coexistence of undernutrition and overweight/obesity (double burden of malnutrition). Public-health texts also call coexistence of communicable and non-communicable diseases the 'dual/double burden of disease'.

statements.t: The dual burden in Indian public health is rising rates of both infectious and non-communicable diseases.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Per the key the dual burden meant is obesity + malnutrition; communicable+NCD is the 'double burden of disease'.

statements.t: The dual burden in Indian public health is overburdened doctors and infrastructure.
The dual burden in Indian public health is lack of insurance and financial access.
The dual burden in Indian public health is high rates of both obesity and malnutrition.

official_questions.rule: Double burden of malnutrition = under + over nutrition; double burden of disease = CD + NCD.
official_questions.key_note: Option 1 is also a standard meaning ('dual burden of disease'; the app's own notes use it). Key (obesity + malnutrition) kept.

official_questions.stem: The concept of sustainable development was first popularized by which report ?
official_questions.core_fact: The WCED (Brundtland Commission) report 'Our Common Future' (1987) popularised sustainable development: meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.

statements.t: Sustainable development was first popularised by the UNDP Report 1992.
Sustainable development was first popularised by the World Bank Report 1985.
Sustainable development was first popularised by the Brundtland Commission Report 1987.
Sustainable development was first popularised by the Rio Declaration 1992.
statements.fact: Rio (1992) built on the 1987 Brundtland concept.

official_questions.rule: 1972 Stockholm -> 1987 Brundtland -> 1992 Rio -> 2015 SDGs.

official_questions.stem: What is a key goal of sustainable development ?
options: Economic growth with no concern for environmental impacts
Ensuring social equity, economic growth and environmental protection
Promoting environmental conservation over all else
official_questions.key: Ensuring social equity, economic growth and environmental protection
official_questions.core_fact: Sustainable development balances economic growth, social equity and environmental protection.

statements.t: A key goal of sustainable development is economic growth with no concern for environmental impacts.
A key goal of sustainable development is ensuring social equity, economic growth and environmental protection.
statements.d: social equity, economic growth and environmental protection

statements.t: A key goal of sustainable development is limiting global population growth.
statements.fact: Population is one factor, not the goal.

statements.t: A key goal of sustainable development is promoting environmental conservation over all else.
statements.fact: SD balances environment with economy and society.

official_questions.rule: SD = economy + society + environment together; watch 'only', 'over all else'.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is not one of the three pillars of sustainability ?
official_questions.core_fact: The three pillars are environmental, economic and social sustainability ('people, planet, profit').

statements.t: Environmental sustainability is not one of the three pillars of sustainability.
Economic sustainability is not one of the three pillars of sustainability.
Social sustainability is not one of the three pillars of sustainability.
Political sustainability is not one of the three pillars of sustainability.

official_questions.rule: Three pillars: environment, economy, society (sometimes culture/governance as a fourth).

official_questions.stem: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) has the United Nations established ?
official_questions.core_fact: UN 2030 Agenda (Sept 2015) has 17 SDGs and 169 targets.

statements.t: The UN has established 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
The UN has established 10 Sustainable Development Goals.
The UN has established 12 Sustainable Development Goals.
The UN has established 20 Sustainable Development Goals.

official_questions.stem: Subject that is not associated with Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the "Circular Economy" ?
options: It focuses on reducing the use of fossil fuels
It promotes the reuse, recycling and repair of materials to reduce waste
It focuses exclusively on reducing carbon emissions
official_questions.key: It promotes the reuse, recycling and repair of materials to reduce waste
official_questions.core_fact: A circular economy keeps materials in use through reduce, reuse, repair, refurbish and recycle, replacing the linear take-make-dispose model.

statements.t: The circular economy focuses on reducing the use of fossil fuels.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: That is decarbonisation; circular economy is about material loops.

statements.t: The circular economy promotes reuse, recycling and repair of materials to reduce waste.
The circular economy encourages linear economic growth.
statements.fact: Circular economy replaces the linear model.

statements.t: The circular economy focuses exclusively on reducing carbon emissions.

official_questions.stem: Which global summit led to the adoption of the "Agenda 21" and the "Rio Declaration" ?
official_questions.core_fact: UNCED (Earth Summit), Rio de Janeiro, June 1992 adopted Agenda 21, the Rio Declaration and Forest Principles, and opened UNFCCC and CBD for signature.

statements.t: The Kyoto Protocol led to the adoption of Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration.
statements.fact: Kyoto (1997) is a UNFCCC protocol; Agenda 21 came from Rio 1992.

statements.t: The Earth Summit 1992 led to the adoption of Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration.

The World Health Assembly 2000 led to the adoption of Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration.

official_questions.rule: Rio 1992: Agenda 21, Rio Declaration, UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD process; Rio+20 2012: 'The Future We Want'.

Ayushman Bharat primarily aims to provide healthcare coverage to rural and poor populations.
Ayushman Bharat primarily aims to provide healthcare coverage to senior citizens.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following factors contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India ?
options: Lack of access to clean water
Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
official_questions.key: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
official_questions.core_fact: Inadequate diets and household food insecurity (with poor feeding practices) are the main immediate drivers of malnutrition in India; WASH and disease are contributory.

statements.t: Lack of access to clean water contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: WASH contributes via infections but diet/food insecurity is the main driver.

statements.t: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India.
statements.d: Poor dietary habits and food insecurity

statements.t: Overconsumption of processed foods contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Processed foods drive obesity, not the main undernutrition burden.

statements.t: Increase in environmental pollution contributed most to the burden of malnutrition in India.
statements.fact: Pollution is not the main malnutrition driver.

official_questions.rule: Immediate causes of malnutrition: diet + disease; underlying: food insecurity, care, WASH.

statements.fact: Malaria is spread by female Anopheles.

official_questions.rule: Mosquito: malaria, dengue, chikungunya, filaria, JE, zika; sandfly: kala-azar; tsetse: sleeping sickness.

official_questions.stem: Reason for the melting of Gangothri glaciers of Himalayas
official_questions.core_fact: Retreat of Gangotri (and other Himalayan glaciers) is attributed mainly to global warming (rising temperatures), with black carbon/dust deposition as an aggravating factor.

statements.t: The reason for the melting of the Gangotri glacier is global warming.
The reason for the melting of the Gangotri glacier is chlorofluorocarbons.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: CFCs are linked to ozone depletion; the direct cause is warming.

statements.t: The reason for the melting of the Gangotri glacier is particulate dust.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Dust/black carbon aggravate melting but the main reason is global warming.

statements.t: The reason for the melting of the Gangotri glacier is greenhouse gases.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

official_questions.rule: Glacier retreat <- global warming <- GHGs; BC/dust lower albedo.
official_questions.key_note: 'Greenhouse gases' is the underlying cause of the same warming; key (global warming) kept.

official_questions.stem:

Reason (R) : Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are man made gases used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays.
options: (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
official_questions.key: (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.core_fact: CFCs are potent greenhouse gases and ozone-depleting substances (more UV reaching the surface); they are man-made refrigerants, AC coolants and aerosol propellants (phased out by Montreal Protocol).

statements.t: CFCs are greenhouse gases that contribute to climate change and increase UV radiation on earth.
CFCs are man-made gases used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays.
(CFCs are man-made gases used in refrigerators, air conditioners and aerosol sprays) explains why (CFCs are greenhouse gases that contribute to climate change and increase UV radiation on earth).
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Their uses (R) explain their release, not their radiative/ozone-depleting properties (A).

official_questions.rule: CFC: GHG + ODS; uses != mechanism.

official_questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement.
options: CO2 is continuously being released because of human activities
Deforestation is decreasing the amount of CO2
Oil spillage causes oxygen depletion and distress to aquatic animals
Burning of plastic reduces the germination of seeds in crop fields
official_questions.key: Deforestation is decreasing the amount of CO2
official_questions.core_fact: Human activities continuously release CO2; deforestation increases atmospheric CO2 (lost sink + burning); oil spills deplete oxygen and harm aquatic life; burning plastics releases toxins harmful to soil and seed germination.

statements.t: CO2 is continuously being released because of human activities.
Deforestation is decreasing the amount of CO2.
Oil spillage causes oxygen depletion and distress to aquatic animals.
Burning of plastic reduces the germination of seeds in crop fields.

official_questions.rule: Forests = sink; deforestation = source (~10% of emissions).

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
a. India's overall SDG score has improved to 71 in 2023-24, Uttarakhand shares the top spot with Kerala, both scored above India's overall SDG score.
b. In the latest SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh is placed in the "Front Runner" category.
c. Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, each with scores above 75, are placed in the "Achiever" category.
d. In the 2023-2024 SDG Index, Lakshadweep and Uttar Pradesh scored significantly above the national average, demonstrating notable progress compared to other states.
official_questions.core_fact: NITI Aayog SDG India Index 2023-24 (12 July 2024): India's composite score 71 (66 in 2020-21); Kerala and Uttarakhand top (79); categories Aspirant 0-49, Performer 50-64, Front Runner 65-99, Achiever 100 - no state reached Achiever; Bihar lowest (57).

statements.t: India's overall SDG score improved to 71 in 2023-24; Uttarakhand shares the top spot with Kerala, both above India's score.
In SDG India Index 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh is placed in the Front Runner category.
Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya, each scoring above 75, are placed in the Achiever category.
statements.fact: No state/UT reached the Achiever category (score 100) in 2023-24; these NE states were in lower bands with scores well below 75.

statements.t: In 2023-24, Lakshadweep and Uttar Pradesh scored significantly above the national average.
statements.fact: Uttar Pradesh (about 67) scored below the national 71; neither was 'significantly above' the average.

official_questions.rule: SDG India Index: bands Aspirant/Performer/Front Runner/Achiever; 2023-24 top Kerala & Uttarakhand, bottom Bihar.
official_questions.key_note: Key 'a, b only' kept; exact scores of the NE states in c are not verified here, the Achiever-band fact settles c.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is a potential tipping point of global climate change ?
official_questions.core_fact: Arctic sea-ice loss is a recognised tipping element (ice-albedo feedback); others: Greenland/West Antarctic ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon dieback, permafrost.

statements.t: Loss of Arctic ice is a potential tipping point of global climate change.
Reduction in CO2 emissions is a potential tipping point of global climate change.
Increased deforestation is a potential tipping point of global climate change.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Deforestation is a driver; the tipping element is Amazon dieback.

statements.t: Decrease in solar radiation is a potential tipping point of global climate change.

official_questions.rule: Tipping elements: sea ice, ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, permafrost, coral reefs.

official_questions.core_fact: The (Antarctic) ozone hole is caused mainly by chlorine and bromine from CFCs and halons, which destroy stratospheric ozone catalytically on polar stratospheric clouds.

statements.t: The ozone hole is primarily caused by the release of carbon dioxide.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The ozone hole is primarily caused by the release of chlorofluorocarbons.
The ozone hole is primarily caused by the release of nitrous oxide.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: N2O depletes ozone but the ozone hole was caused chiefly by CFCs.

statements.t: The ozone hole is primarily caused by the release of methane.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Methane is a GHG, not the ozone-hole cause.

official_questions.rule: Ozone hole -> CFCs/halons; warming -> CO2/CH4/N2O.

official_questions.stem: Which International Agreement does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change ?
official_questions.core_fact: Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement target GHG emissions; Montreal Protocol (ODS) addresses HFC greenhouse gases via the Kigali Amendment (2016); Basel Convention (1989) controls trans-boundary hazardous waste.

statements.t: The Montreal Protocol does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

statements.t: The Kyoto Protocol does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
statements.fact: Kyoto set binding GHG cuts for Annex I.

statements.t: The Paris Agreement does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
statements.fact: Paris is the core GHG treaty.

statements.t: The Basel Convention does not focus on reducing greenhouse gas emissions.

official_questions.rule: Basel = hazardous waste; Rotterdam = PIC; Stockholm = POPs; Montreal = ODS (+HFCs).
official_questions.key_note: Montreal's primary aim is ozone, but its Kigali Amendment makes it a GHG instrument; key (Basel) unambiguous.

official_questions.rule: NAPCC: 8 missions, 2008; adaptation and mitigation both.
